segments.title: 第19章 溪姐,喝茶
segments.content:
"So you write novels in your spare time, and that's why your composition scores are so good?"

"Right."

"And then you published the novel you wrote on someone's platform, and their editor took a liking to it?"

"Right."

"Now they're inviting you to become a contracted author, and after you sign the contract, you'll have a chance to earn money?"

"Right."

"But a minor needs a guardian's consent to sign a contract, is that what you mean?"

"Right."

"Are there any problems with this kind of contract? Will signing it affect your studies in the future?"

"These are all standard contracts, fixed templates. All new authors sign them this way," Li Luo explained. "And there are no strict obligations. You can write as much as you want, whenever you want. The platform is just responsible for distributing and promoting it for you online to attract readers to your book."

"Oh, okay, I get it now." Lin Xiuhong nodded, pondered for a moment, then looked at Li Luo again. "Then we'll have to make a deal. I can help you sign the contract, but if your grades don't hold up after you start high school, we'll have to revisit this."

"No problem!"

If Li Luo had come to Lin Xiuhong before the high school entrance exams to say he'd written a novel and someone wanted to sign him, she would have rolled her eyes and yanked him by the ear, telling him to get serious and stop messing around with pointless things.

But the Li Luo of today was a completely different person in his parents' eyes.

It wasn't just that he had done extremely well on his entrance exams and gotten a perfect score on the Chinese composition, but also because Li Luo had matured significantly in his words and actions during this time.

Although he still said some outlandish things occasionally, he had grown far, far more than before.

This made Lin Xiuhong feel increasingly assured and at ease with what Li Luo was doing.

Besides, the fact that her son's casual writings could be scouted and offered a contract gave her a bit of a reason to be proud.

But making money from a novel?

Lin Xiuhong wasn't counting on that. For a kid's writing, getting some buzz was good enough.

So when faced with her son's request to sign a contract with the online platform, she simply inquired about the specifics in detail, and after confirming there were no issues, she agreed.

As for writing novels improving his composition skills?

That kind of talk could only fool someone like Lin Xiuhong, with her middle school education...

But regardless, Li Luo, relying on the "reformed prodigal son" persona he had built for over half a month, had finally passed his mom's trial and successfully signed the contract for the first novel of his new life.

*I'm Really Not a Star* had its contract status successfully updated in the following days and entered the normal recommendation process.

By the next Sunday, under the arrangement of his editor Qian Zhou, Li Luo's novel appeared on the recommendation list for the Urban category on Qidian.

Li Luo himself also welcomed the school promotion banquet his family had arranged for him after his exams.

...

The school promotion banquet was something Li Luo had never actually experienced in his previous life.

After all, he nearly ended up in a vocational high school after the entrance exams. His parents had to pay a school selection fee just to get him into a regular high school, a record that wasn't exactly worth celebrating.

His college entrance exam results were just as unsightly. Again, he had to rely on his parents' connections to get into a local junior college where he learned some culinary skills, which at least saved him from starvation.

Thus, the so-called school promotion banquet was never something he was destined for.

"Did your dad not plan on throwing a school promotion banquet for you?"

At just past three in the afternoon, as the family was preparing to leave for the restaurant, Li Luo asked Ying Chanxi while they were heading downstairs.

"Dad is too busy. I just told him to focus on work. A school promotion banquet isn't necessary." Ying Chanxi shook her head, walking beside Li Luo, then said with a charming smile, "Besides, aren't I here to mooch off your school promotion banquet? We can just pretend I had one too."

"That's true," Li Luo nodded. "But with your grades, if my parents were to throw a banquet for you, anything less than ten or twenty tables wouldn't do justice to your status as number one in the entire district."

"You're exaggerating," Ying Chanxi shot him a look.

The two followed Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong downstairs. Zhao Rongjun, who had been invited to the banquet, was already waiting for them.

While Li Guohong went to get the car, Li Luo placed one hand on Ying Chanxi's shoulder and slung his other arm around Zhao Rongjun's neck, sighing, "To be honest, you two are the last people I wanted to see at my school promotion banquet."

"Why?" Zhao Rongjun looked completely baffled. "Didn't you only invite the two of us from school?"

"Isn't that because I'm closest with you two?" Li Luo clicked his tongue, then continued, "When the time comes, my relatives will praise me, saying, 'Li Luo is so amazing, he actually scored 555 on the entrance exams! He got into Fu Yi Zhong.'"

"Then the relatives will turn to my two dear classmates and ask how you two did."

"Turns out, you're both freaks who got into Fu Yi Zhong through independent admissions."

"My attempt at showing off gets shut down halfway. You think I won't feel miserable?"

Ying Chanxi beside him slapped his hand away and said with a disdainful side-eye, "You're so childish."

"You don't get it." Li Luo wagged his finger. "If you're not childish now, when you grow up, you won't have the environment or the conditions to be childish anymore."

"Don't just stand there chatting, get in the car!" Li Guohong drove the second-hand sedan out of the garage and called for them to get in.

Lin Xiuhong took the front passenger seat, and the three kids piled into the back.

Zhao Rongjun was very considerate and took the seat by the door, leaving the middle seat for Li Luo.

Ying Chanxi sat on Li Luo's other side.

Because Zhao Rongjun was so husky, and the back seat of the small sedan wasn't spacious, Li Luo was squeezed over toward Ying Chanxi. He had to sit pressed up against her to barely fit.

Ying Chanxi didn't seem to mind this at all. She simply rolled down the window to let the breeze in, making the back seat less stuffy.

"Actually, my spot is the most dangerous one in the whole car," Li Luo said from the middle of the back seat with a deadpan expression. "So, Dad, drive carefully."

"You sure have a lot to say," Li Guohong chuckled, then added, "Your third grand-uncle's family is coming this time. Do you remember what I told you last time?"

"Hm? What was it?" Li Luo paused, then it hit him, and his brows lifted slightly. "Is it about Third Grand-uncle's apartment?"

"Yes." Li Guohong said with a smile, "This time, besides celebrating your school promotion, the main reason is to invite your third grand-uncle and his family over to discuss buying the apartment."

"Why the sudden decision to buy an apartment?" Li Luo asked curiously. "What about my cousin's situation?"

"Let's put that on hold for now," Li Guohong said. "As for buying the apartment... well, it's been decided."

Although the decision was made because Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong were moved by their son's progress and growth after his good exam results, Li Guohong decided not to tell him, afraid the kid would get too cocky.

After Li Guohong spoke, Lin Xiuhong beside him added, "That apartment is right next to Fu Yi Zhong. If we're quick, the transfer can be done during the summer break."

"Your third grand-uncle's apartment is usually rented out to Fu Yi Zhong students, so the rooms and everything are all set up."

"When you and Xixi go to Fu Yi Zhong, you won't have to squeeze into a dorm, and you won't have to wake up super early every day to catch the bus from home."

"This way, it'll be more convenient for you to get to school, and you'll sleep more comfortably. I can come over on the weekends to cook for you all. How great is that!"

Hearing Lin Xiuhong's words, Ying Chanxi in the back seat blinked and asked Lin Xiuhong in a small voice, "Auntie Lin, if you buy the apartment, can I... can I live there too? Wouldn't that be imposing?"

"What's there to impose?" Lin Xiuhong's tone held a hint of displeasure. "Xixi, are you still being so formal with us? If you talk like that, you'll hurt my feelings."

"No, no! It's just... it's just..." Ying Chanxi waved her hands frantically, not knowing how to express herself.

At that moment, Li Guohong interrupted them, turning instead to Zhao Rongjun. "Xiao Jun too, actually. You two have helped Li Luo so much. You can both live with us. It'll be more convenient for school."

"Oh, thank you, Uncle." Zhao Rongjun said quickly. "But my grandpa's house is quite close to the school, so I'll be staying there."

"What about Xixi then?" Li Guohong now turned to Ying Chanxi. "I'll talk to your dad about it later. You can just move right in. It'd be perfect, you can help Uncle and Auntie keep an eye on this kid, Li Luo."

"After all, if he lives alone outside of school, your auntie and I have to run the breakfast shop and won't have time to watch him."

"If he reverts to his old ways and starts messing around, your auntie and I would have no way of knowing."

"But if you're there, and he dares to not study hard, you can tattle on him to us, and I'll have your Auntie Lin deal with him."

After that speech, Ying Chanxi suddenly found she could accept this kind offer. Her gaze towards Li Luo even held a hint of smugness and anticipation, which left Li Luo speechless.

"What do you mean 'reverts to his old ways'? Dad, you have a high school diploma and you're pulling out words like that?" Li Luo couldn't help but retort.

"Aren't you getting nosy? I'm the person with the highest diploma in this car right now, you know," Li Guohong scoffed.

The corner of Li Luo's mouth twitched. "Dad, that's a bit shameless of you."

"Anyway, we'll see if we can get the transfer for your third grand-uncle's apartment done sooner," Li Guohong rolled his eyes. "Once the apartment is settled, if you live there, someone definitely needs to keep an eye on you."

"Honestly, Ying Chanxi's father might not even agree."

"What if you affect Xixi's studies? With Xixi's grades, she can pick any university she wants in the future. She's much more precious than you."

"Not at all, not at all." Ying Chanxi quickly waved her hands in modesty. "Uncle Li, you're exaggerating. Just leave the task of watching Li Luo to me. No problem!"

"Good, good, then it's settled." Lin Xiuhong laughed happily.

The atmosphere in the small car suddenly became exceptionally cheerful. Before long, Li Guohong arrived at the restaurant entrance.

It was only around four in the afternoon, so the guests hadn't arrived yet.

Li Guohong's group arrived first, sat down in the private room, and went over the menu again.

The restaurant's owner, Lin Shufen, also came in, holding Lin Xiuhong's hand with a beaming smile as they reminisced.

"Is this your son? I haven't seen Li Luo in so long. Do you still remember me?" Lin Shufen greeted Li Luo with a chuckle.

"Hello, Auntie." Li Luo honestly couldn't make sense of the vast web of relatives on both his parents' sides. At this moment, he could only activate his memory palace, search for a bit, and then take the initiative. "You held me when I was little, how could I not remember."

"Haha~ You even remember me holding you?" Lin Shufen laughed heartily, unable to resist mentioning, "Then do you remember you peed on me while I was holding you?"

"Yes, yes." Lin Xiuhong beside them also burst out laughing, slapping her thigh, roaring with her cousin as she recalled Li Luo's childhood. "He was still wearing open-crotch pants back then, crying his eyes out while peeing."

"Mom." Li Luo's face darkened as he listened, and he quickly cut in, "Let's not bring that up again. You might as well talk more about my entrance exam scores."

"Why can't we bring it up?" Ying Chanxi piped up from the side. "I think it's very interesting."

"You shut up too," Li Luo glared at Ying Chanxi, annoyed.

Ying Chanxi shot him a sideways glance, not the least bit afraid of his glare. Instead, she twirled a strand of hair by her ear and said slowly, "I still remember a lot of your embarrassing moments from elementary school, for example..."

"Sister Xi, have some tea, have some tea." Li Luo quickly poured Ying Chanxi a cup of tea. "The weather is really nice today, right, Xiao Jun?"

Zhao Rongjun blinked, then said, "Actually, I also know about your elementary school..."

"Brother Jun! Brother Jun!" Li Luo gritted his teeth and offered this guy a cup of tea as well.

"Ahem, Li Luo." Lin Xiuhong tapped the table lightly. "Don't you see your auntie doesn't have any tea either?"

"No need, no need, I should be the one pouring for you all," Lin Shufen's face crinkled with laughter, thoroughly amused.

But Li Luo had already stood up obediently and poured tea for his auntie too.

This school promotion banquet had turned him into a waiter before the first dish was even served.

But just as he finished pouring tea for his mom and auntie and sat back down, Ying Chanxi beside him poured a cup of tea and pushed it in front of him.

"Here, you have some too."
